nodes.question: Does the edited image visibly show the source paper stuffed inside the source cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass only when the edited image provides enough evidence that the paper is inside the cup and has been stuffed into it, not merely resting on the rim. Fail only when the paper and cup can be identified and the paper is visibly outside or merely on the rim. Otherwise return unknown. Compare plausible visual continuity across source and edit using shape, material, color, and scene context; allow appearance changes, but do not treat resemblance or overlap alone as proof of identity or completion.
nodes.binding: Anchor the paper and cup to the source objects. The source shows a white sheet and blue cup; use contextual visual continuity to assess whether edited objects could be those objects, without requiring exact appearance matching or assuming identity when uncertain.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show the source paper being folded, crumpled, or otherwise compressed as it is inserted into the source cup?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if visible evidence supports both insertion into the cup and stuffing or compression of the paper. Fail only if the relevant paper and cup are identifiable and the image affirmatively shows no such insertion or compression. Otherwise return unknown. Inspect the paper's shape and its spatial relation to the cup opening; proximity or contact alone is insufficient. Use plausible contextual continuity across source and edit, allowing appearance changes without assuming identity.
nodes.binding: Assess the requested stuffing of the source-image paper into the source-image cup. The source shows a white sheet and blue cup; contextual continuity may support identity despite changed appearance, but resemblance alone does not establish it.

nodes.question: Does the edited image show progress toward stuffing the source paper into the source cup, short of completion?
nodes.criteria: Pass only if the image shows an action or placement that advances the paper into the cup, and s1 has not established completion. Fail only if the paper and cup can be identified and the image affirmatively shows no progress toward insertion, or s1 establishes completion. Otherwise return unknown. Compare plausible visual continuity across source and edit using shape, material, color, and scene context while allowing appearance changes. Proximity, overlap, or a hand holding paper alone does not establish progress; uncertain identity or action does not establish absence of progress.
nodes.binding: Progress must concern stuffing the source-image paper into the source-image cup. Allow contextual continuity despite appearance changes, but do not infer identity or progress from resemblance or proximity alone.

program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. You receive no reference label or optimization feedback. Return status, evidence, reported confidence (0..1 or null), and used_dependency_ids naming every supplied context check_id exactly once in saved order.
Supports receive source and edited images. Answer only the saved proposition using its binding and criteria. Use pass/fail/unknown. Context is advisory unless listed in required_dependencies. A negative context observation is usable evidence. Unknown, skipped, or invalid context is not a failure and must not stop an independent image inspection. Inspect the images yourself; do not repeat a parent's answer. Return unknown when the relevant fact cannot be established. Confidence reports confidence in this answer, not calibrated correctness.
Fulfillment receives NO images. Use only saved support evidence, original instruction/rubric and frozen composition criteria. Return complete/partial/absent/unknown. Supporting passes answer specific propositions, not a count of completed edits. Their polarity can differ. Apply saved alternatives: optional uncertainty need not prevent a known outcome, but a required unresolved fact makes that outcome unresolved. Never invent a visual fact or convert missing evidence into failure. A conditional skip is not non-applicability. All applicable requested outcomes complete gives yes; no requested progress gives no; known progress short of completion gives partial. Unrelated changes are not progress.
